Project Report

Water Delivery Tracker

This report captures the progression of the iOS class project built in SwiftUI and SwiftData for tracking residential or condo water deliveries, cumulative meter readings, tank forecasts, vendor contact info, and operational planning.

Primary use case: one tracked location such as Merritt House, with a configurable tank capacity, refill tracking, missed-reading recovery, and forecasting for reserve and runout timing.

Tracking integration

Current scope

  • One location profile with editable name, tank settings, vendor info, and baseline values.
  • History logging for meter checks, full-fill deliveries, and gallons-delivered events.
  • Observed tank percentage fallback for missed delivery or missed reading situations.
  • Dashboard forecast for current tank estimate, reserve timing, and out-of-water timing.
  • Monthly and daily usage summaries driven from cumulative meter progression.

Feature progression

1. Initial starter app

Started as a beginner-friendly SwiftUI app with a dashboard, settings, and history flow using local persistence so it could be pasted into Xcode and run as a class project.

2. Delivery model correction

The original assumption of always knowing gallons delivered was replaced with a more realistic model that supports Filled To Full for top-off deliveries, because many real-world deliveries only confirm that the tank was topped off.

3. Dual delivery modes

The model was expanded to support both Filled To Full and Gallons Delivered, allowing different vendors or record quality over time.

4. Strict delivery rule

Delivery entries were aligned with the decision that delivery events should require a same-day meter reading for clean and reliable forecasting.

5. Better starting baseline

The app was updated to start from both a cumulative starting meter value and the current gallons in the tank so the first forecast and usage calculations have a reliable starting anchor.

6. Form usability improvements

Settings were updated to show visible labels above fields instead of relying only on placeholder text that disappears once values are entered.

7. Recovery path for missed readings

An observed tank level dropdown in 10% increments was added so a user can manually re-anchor the tank state when one or more deliveries or readings were missed.

8. Location-aware UX

A location name such as Merritt House was added to settings so the main page can display a meaningful property name instead of only a generic app title.

9. Tealium tracking hooks

A TrackingService.swift helper was added to wrap Tealium view and event tracking for dashboard views, history actions, vendor call taps, and settings updates.

Key product decisions

  • One location first: keeps the class project manageable and easier to understand.
  • SwiftData: chosen so records persist between launches without building a custom storage layer.
  • Forecasting rule: reserve warning and estimated runout date are both surfaced.
  • Real-world flexibility: delivery logging supports both complete and incomplete operational data.
  • Tracking wrapper: Tealium is initialized once in a shared helper instead of being called directly from every screen.

Current event model

Event typeWhat it means
Meter Check OnlyRecords a cumulative meter reading without changing the tank by a delivery action.
Filled To FullRecords a delivery where the tank is known to have been topped off to full capacity.
Gallons DeliveredRecords a delivery where a measured delivery amount is known and should be added to the tank level.
Observed Tank LevelOptional manual anchor that sets the estimated tank volume using 10% increments of the configured capacity.

How the calculations work now

  • Usage: based on the difference between cumulative meter readings, similar to an odometer.
  • Starting point: the app begins from a starting meter reading plus current gallons in the system.
  • Filled To Full delivery: the tank estimate resets to the configured full capacity.
  • Gallons Delivered delivery: the tank estimate increases by the logged delivery amount, capped at tank capacity.
  • Observed level fallback: when readings or deliveries were missed, the observed percent-to-gallons entry can reset the estimated tank state.
  • Reserve forecast: based on current estimated gallons minus the safety reserve using average daily usage.
  • Runout forecast: based on total estimated gallons divided by average daily usage.

Example operational workflow

Normal delivery day

Enter the date, current meter reading, and select either Filled To Full or Gallons Delivered.

Routine check day

Enter the date and current cumulative meter reading as a meter check only event.

Missed records

If a delivery or reading was missed, use the observed tank percentage dropdown to re-anchor the tank estimate.

Vendor action

Store vendor contact info in Settings so the dashboard can surface a one-tap call action.

Tracking plan

  • Views: dashboard, history, and settings screen visits.
  • Events: meter reading saves, delivery saves, settings updates, vendor call taps, and deletion of logged records.
  • Implementation style: wrapper helper with trackView and trackEvent methods.
  • Compile safety: helper was designed so the app can still build before the Tealium package is linked.

Notes and feedback

  • Good project choice: this is a strong learning app because it has real business logic, forms, persistence, summaries, and forecasting without being too abstract.
  • Best improvement made: moving from a simple gallons-delivered assumption to a mixed real-world delivery model made the app much more useful.
  • Most important technical habit: keep calculation logic centralized in WaterMath.swift so UI files stay readable.
  • Best beginner pattern: separate models, math, and views into different files so each file has one clear job.
  • Best future learning step: add editing of existing events, because that will teach you bindings, state flow, and data updates in SwiftData.

Known constraints and cleanup notes

  • After SwiftData model changes, simulator data may become stale. If the app behaves strangely after schema changes, delete the app from the simulator and rerun it.
  • The app should run against an iPhone simulator, not a build-only device destination in Xcode.
  • If the Tealium package is not yet installed, the tracking helper should remain safe but will not send live tracking until the SDK and config values are added.
  • If meter readings are missing on delivery events, forecasting becomes weaker, so the observed tank percent fallback is valuable for recovery.

Overall assessment: the project has evolved from a simple learning app into a practical operations tracker with realistic data entry constraints, a clean growth path, and a strong structure for learning SwiftUI, SwiftData, and SDK instrumentation.
